subject.title: Steer mode does not inject messages mid-turn for main sessions

question: Should #89238, or a refreshed successor, become the canonical fix for ordinary same-session messages reaching active-run queue policy during active turns, or should OpenClaw limit mid-turn steering to explicit control commands for now?
rationale: The remaining behavior is not just a local guard bug; it changes where ordinary channel messages bypass serialization and how session routing and fallback delivery behave while a turn is active.

options.title: Adopt the #89238 admission-layer direction
options.body: Refresh and finish the existing candidate so ordinary same-session visible turns can reach active-run queue policy with explicit tests for fallback and session routing.

options.title: Keep command-only steering
options.body: Treat /steer and equivalent control commands as the supported mid-turn path and close or narrow the ordinary-message expectation.

options.title: Split by channel semantics
options.body: Allow channel-specific ingress bypasses only where ordering, threading, and fallback behavior are proven safe, leaving broader concurrency for a later design.

recommendation.title: Adopt the #89238 admission-layer direction
recommendation.body: Refresh and finish the existing candidate so ordinary same-session visible turns can reach active-run queue policy with explicit tests for fallback and session routing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent ownership in reply dispatch and active-run queue surfaces makes this the best available product/architecture routing owner from the history sampled.
